criteria.idempotent_writes: Writes may run as hedged replicas provided every write is idempotent and every read-after-write reconciles by reread: duplicate execution collapses through idempotency, only the winning value reaches the response, and an expired replica keeps reporting commit unknown with supervisor escalation instead of asserting rollback or success.
criteria.reads_only: Only reads without side effects may run as hedged replicas, and writes are never hedged: whenever the primary misses the hedge delay both replicas execute, so hedging a write would apply it twice, and the contract rules writes out by construction rather than reviewing every call site for idempotency.

hedge_effects.instructions: What effects may replicas of one hedged request perform?

criteria.owner_observed: The owner of the hedge keeps full responsibility for loser observation through per-replica fates and settledAll, and the shared sink keeps recording exactly the genuine boundary expiries as escalation records with seq-linked late records. When a loser rejects after the win without expiring its boundary, no sink record exists and the owner observation is the complete account.
criteria.supervised_diagnostic: At the hedge win, hand each unfinished loser to a supervisor scope that owns it separately and emits correlated diagnostics for its late failures. This builds supervised-loser lifetime and shutdown machinery of the O2 design ahead of any W5 leg that would require it.

loser_observation.instructions: Once the winning replica has answered, where should observation of the losing replica live?

criteria.failure_dominates: Surface the known failure whenever some replica rejected and none settled, even alongside an expired sibling: the concrete error identifies an actionable fault, and the expired sibling remains owned with its eventual settlement still reaching the sink without altering the surfaced failure.
criteria.unknown_dominates: Surface the honest unknown-write outcome whenever some replica expired and none settled, even alongside a rejected sibling: the expired replica might have committed, no known failure can settle that commit question, and the unknown marker with supervisor escalation therefore outranks the reported failure.

terminal_precedence.instructions: If the hedge ends with no settled replica and with expiry beside rejection, which outcome should surface?

state: Can compiles to TypeScript adapters that execute natively on Bun 1.4.2. Its completed O1 lifetime layer (E04) consists of: a single shared budget per request where each operation races min(its bound, remaining budget); one frozen unknown-write marker (commit unknown, owned, supervisor escalation) used identically by SQL, fetch, action, S3, and worker paths; the raceBoundary operation boundary that answers with the marker at expiry while native work continues owned until settlement; automatically filed escalation records per expiry carrying budget, disconnect, shutdown, or cancel causes; late records linked by sequence number that observe settlement after expiry; one operation scope per request fitted by dispatch, expiring on disconnect and shutdown; leases immune to timers; and drain-by-default close semantics under which the scope drain ahead of the response waits for owner-admitted native groups. Native meanings come from executed probes: Bun.SQL Query.cancel only flips a client-side flag on PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite while each backend completes, hence SQL follows the cancel-absent branch as bare promises with pool leases and no owner group; fetch aborts natively on AbortSignal, hence the server HTTP client follows the cancel-present branch with owner-admitted native groups. The E05 hedge harness pairs exactly two replicas, each inside its own raceBoundary against the common scope: the primary launches immediately, the secondary launches after hedgeDelayMs unless the primary has already won, the earliest settled replica wins and supplies the handler response value, and the loser never blocks the answer. With abortLosers enabled, every still-pending cancelable loser is aborted at the win via a dedicated controller feeding both its raceBoundary signal and its native abort; SQL replicas declare cancelable false and invariably run owned to settlement. Fifteen legs H0-H12 exercised this shape across genuine loopback HTTP with a stall-injection upstream and live PostgreSQL 17.11 and MySQL 8.4.11 inside isolated database can_e05_run1: H1 answers with the winner below 1500ms next to a two-second group-free loser and files nothing; H2 survives an early replica failure through the secondary; H3 answers unknown-write when every replica expires, with two budget escalations and two seq-linked late settlements; H4 shows fetch replicas without loser abort carrying winner content yet detained near two seconds by loser drain; H5 shows fetch replicas with loser abort answering below 1500ms with the abort visible serve-side plus a cancel escalation and seq-linked late rejection; H6 shows a loser rejection 500ms past the win visible to the hedge owner alone and absent from the sink; H7 shows disconnect expiring both replica boundaries as disconnect with both operations settling owned; H8 stop and H9 SIGTERM child runs bound the live peer as unknown shutdown with clean exit; H10 shows an in-process pool lease at 1 beyond the response, close pausing near 800ms for the lease, then leases at 0 with state closed and later use rejected; H11 and H12 repeat bounded answers, lease 1-then-0, backend sleeper 1-then-0, and concurrent pool use on live PG and MySQL. Binding interface rules demand finite explicit failure unions, a single unknown-write vocabulary, no caller operand lacking a verified native meaning, and zero native causes inside records; the E06 request hook covers unexpected handler failures alone and never drains escalation collections; no universal latency SLO is asserted, only bounded-versus-unbounded orderings. Zero external users exist, so nothing owes compatibility.
